title: Chapter 2. Ramananda Raya's family; Ramananda leaves royal service and comes to Sri Chaitanya; Prataparudra at Kashi Mishra's house
html:
Translated from Odia without a native speaker; doubtful places are marked (?) and (??). The original, transliteration and word-for-word translation are in the full edition (in preparation).

The second vritta (?) [section]1

2.1In this book, the Mahabhava-prakasha, is the essence that came forth from the lotus mouth of Sri Gauranga.
2.2. How can we, worthless ones, describe it? Know the words of Prabhu's holy mouth to be a firm secret.
2.3. The best [place] of the Panchakroshi of Purushottama-kshetra — its name is Bentapur, most charming.2
2.4. In that village dwell the foremost (?) Karanas (?); all of them serve with the king as panjias.3
2.5. In their family there was one named Bhavananda; he, a Pattanayaka, versed in the shastras (?), held (?) to dharma.4
2.6. His three sons are archers (?); because they served the king, … (??) skilful.5
2.7. Versed in all the shastras, they became intimate (?) with Prataparudra.6
2.8. The eldest son, Dharanidhara, is a great yogi; he kept all the affairs of the village … (??).7
2.9. His brother, Gopinatha Pattanayaka, served wonderfully in the science of government.8
2.10. Know likewise his youngest (?) brother: his name is Ramananda Pattanayaka.9
2.11. He, gathering a retinue, took leave (?) and came to govern Vidyanagara.10
2.12. Thus he made arrangements (??) with the king, and thus with dignity he managed a part of the kingdom.11
2.13. Ramananda obtained the rank of Raya; he is the king's dearest friend.12
2.14. His mind is always immersed in the rasa of Krishna; his mind is always attached to Krishna's feet.
2.15. Thus he became mad with the rasa of Krishna and could not manage the affairs (?) of the kingdom.13
2.16. To a brahmana named Bira (??) from the village of Rajyamandri he entrusted his domain.14
2.17. Taking the brahmana Rajiva from the fort of Khallikot, there, on the Godavari (?), he made him his friend (?).15
2.18. In that place Rajiva kept him company (?); he gave words [of instruction] (?) to the pilgrims.16
2.19. Thus Sri Ramananda, intoxicated with the rasa of Krishna, utterly forgot the king's affairs.
2.20. Such a best of devotees could not stay [there]: he heard of Gauranga's Radha-rasa in Sri Kshetra.17
2.21. He ceaselessly chanted the name "Radha, Radha", and handed over (?) [his charge] to King Prataparudra.18
2.22. He left the king's company and joined Chaitanya, immersing his mind in the feet of Guru-Govinda.19
2.23. King Prataparudra, trusting in him, dwells (?) with him, having come to the eternal abode (?).20
2.24. They entered Kashi Mishra's house; the king came and prostrated himself before Prabhu.21
2.25. He said: "We shall hear the command from the holy (??) mouth" …22
2.26. At the root of an amalaki (?) tree Chaitanya Thakura, seated, at once (?) manifested bhava.23
2.27. "Rise, rise, O king!" [He] cried out; Ramananda Raya lifted the king and held him up.24
2.28. All the devotees became one-pointed, all fixing their meditation on the feet of Chaitanya Thakura.

Ramananda Raya asks about the tattva of Radha; Mahaprabhu explains the hidden tattva: bijas, sakhis, fire and water; the Goloka story begins

2.29In their souls the maha-mantra of Krishna, in their mouths the great name; with the corners of their eyes [they] behold the feet of Sri Prabhu.
2.30. Thus some time passed in silence; Raya Ramananda, together (?) with the king (?), came before [Prabhu].25
2.31. Joining his hands, raising high (?) … (??), he said: "Please explain [to us] the light of the universe.26
2.32. That Radha who is … (??) of Vrishabhanu, the beloved (?) of Krishna, who is the great shakti flooding (?) the world —27
2.33. please explain to us (??) the tattva of that Radha. Hearing this mahabhava, may [our] lives be blessed."28
2.34. Hearing this, Prabhu smiled; Prabhu cried aloud [about] the tattva (?) of Radha and Krishna.29
2.35. He uttered the names "Krishna, Krishna, Radha, Radha" and, half-closing His eyes, revealed the great tattva:
2.36. "Listen (?), O devotees, to what you have asked: you have asked about the deepest secret of all the Vaishnava shastras.30
2.37. Know, then: this is a hidden tattva; know, O devotees, this is the unmanifest lila.31
2.38. The fifty (?) letters, which are light — in the same way (?) they, comprising the tattvas of all the mantras, are of infinite measure.32
2.39. Among them are the bijas of all the gods; 'ram', O servant (?), is the bija of Radhika.33
2.40. The letter 'ra' is the embodiment of the great radiance; the letter 'ra', know, is the supreme … …34
2.41. Radhika is the form of the radiance of fire; by the bija 'ram' prema … becoming … (??) to Krishna.35
2.42. In the essential structure (?) of the body all abide; by the eight letters the eight sakhis surround [Her].36
2.43. The bija 'lam' (?) is fire by nature, its place is in the heart; know: [She] is the ruler of the heart's … (??), the form of prema.37
2.44. She is the ruler of the pingala channel; She, full of prema, showers the nectar of prema.38
2.45. Lalita, Vishakha, Chandralekha and the other sakhis — see — have surrounded the bijas … (??).39
2.46. … (??) — Radha is like fire; know: She is not born of a womb.40
2.47. Radhika is fire, and the Yamuna is water; She is the heat of fire, ever longing.41
2.48. Ever restless with the radiance of fire, [They] keep sporting in the waters of the Yamuna.42
2.49. The secret of the tattva of kama they know without knowing; the tattvas of play they contemplate in the mind.43
2.50. She abides in all places; [She] whose treasure (?) is the jewel (?) abiding in the circle of the Void.44
2.51. As a lotus leaf, though in water, [remains] to the water … (?): [the drops] roll about, … (??) does not stick … (??);45
2.52. as pure gold melts in fire, [while] a jewel remains [in water] — and even deep within (?) the water does not pass into it;46
2.53. as the bee kisses the madhavi flower — having kissed the flower, the bee flies off [taking (?)] the honey —47
2.54. so too Radha's body has no touch: in union with the radiance of 'ram' Krishna joyfully sports.48
2.55. Such is Prabhu's account. …49
2.56. In Goloka Sri Radha became angry on account of Sudama; the son of Nanda Himself … 50

Radha's anger and Kishora's distress; Radha as Yogamaya and Bhavamayi; the secret of bhava; the search for a guru and the meeting with Keshava Bharati

2.57Seeing the anger of the supreme Shakti, Kishora, the all-auspicious, fell into great distress.51
2.58. They saw the supreme light — Prabhu, the primeval root; all the devotees, in remembrance (?), say:52
2.59. "Since Radha is Yogamaya in the form of a woman, therefore She wears yellow garments.53
2.60. Among proud beauties She is the proud one; among those who walk like an intoxicated [elephant] (?), She is called the one of the finest gait.54
2.61. Among beautiful women She is the most beautiful of all, enchanting Krishna with Her beauty, having assumed a form of radiance.
2.62. Bodiless, She eternally enjoys in a body (?); with the youth of Vraja She sports.55
2.63. Sometimes in a body (?) She bears a body; and again, becoming invisible, She sports with Krishna.
2.64. Radha is a beauty [made] of bhava, the mine of bhava; therefore Her name is Bhavamayi.
2.65. The bhava of the heart, or … (??) — so all call Her; know: this is Radha; hence She bears a secret name.56
2.66. Whoever serves Krishna absorbed in bhava gains [a place] within Radha's body.57
2.67. When, immersed (?) in bhava, one worships Krishna, that is concentration in the mood of Radha's bhava.58
2.68. This bhava is secret; this is an unmanifest bhava; these matters will never become manifest.
2.69. Know these to be secret, esoteric tattvas …"59
2.70. We have expounded the words of our guru; we ourselves have spoken the supreme knowledge.60
2.71. Know this to be the supreme secret teaching; here is the proof: we heard this tattva from the guru's mouth.
2.72. So we shall tell you what is secret, and remove all doubts from your hearts.
2.73. When we came to the Kshetra, [our] body fell in supreme absorption in Krishna.61
2.74. Without a guru this body fell into distress; without a guru the body became futile.
2.75. Without the guru's grace this (?) soul is futile; when there is the guru's grace, the soul gains its purpose (?).62
2.76. Not having obtained such grace (??) of a guru, I grieved; [then] I met a certain Vaishnava on the bank of a lake.63
2.77. His name was Keshava Bharati, a supreme Vaishnava; his bhava ever abides in the rasa of Hari.64
2.78. Seeing my despair, he could not bear it; "We are not worthy (?)," he let me know.65
2.79. I fell, firmly clasping his feet, and said: "Liberate my soul!"
2.80. Thus, seeing me, he became distressed; he lifted me from the ground and seated me (?).66
2.81. Embracing me, he then spoke with sweet speech: …67
2.82. He said: "We indeed know your story; we know: your body is Krishna's secret.68
2.83. We know your mind is always turned to Krishna; thinking (?) of this, we are greatly happy at heart.69
2.84. Supreme service to Krishna is very … …70
2.85. We know only how to receive the guru's grace; I have no command from my guru to give [it] to you."71

Keshava Bharati on Madhavendra Puri; the search for the sadguru among the dunes; initiation; "bhava is the form of Radha"

2.86Our guru is Madhavendra Puri; of all the shastras … …72
2.87. He eternally serves the Supreme Krishna; he always abides (?) in supreme bhava.
2.88. Bathing in the water of the tears from his eyes, he makes the dust of the devotees' feet his tilaka.
2.89. He is ever immersed in the service (?) of Vishnu (?), the Kaivalya; in bhava he obtains the darshan of the Supreme Krishna.73
2.90. Such is my guru — he is [like Mount] Meru; he is the guru of our Bharati ashrama.74
2.91. My ashrama is beside Gupta-Vrindavana, near the [Jagannatha-]vallabha, to the east [of it].75
2.92. There (?) is my meditation and concentration. No one (?) will regard us as your guru.76
2.93. Know: we shall bring you to a sadguru; [he] will reveal (?) all the bhavas."77
2.94. Having said this, we two then set off; coming to the Bharati ashrama, we soon joined [the devotees there] (?).
2.95. All the devotees grew restless; we wandered eagerly, searching for the guru.
2.96. Thus we wandered over the heaps of sand, leaping with great zeal from dune to dune.78
2.97. There was a single ashrama, there a small (?) hut; there Madhavendra Puri practises concentration.79
2.98. Into that place we two entered; prostrating on the ground, we pressed ourselves (?) to [his] feet.80
2.99. Seeing us, the guru lifted [me] up and embraced [me]; breathing in the scent of [my] hair, he seated [me] on his lap.81
2.100. At that moment we directly experienced the bhava of Hari (?); tears streamed from our eyes, and we could not contain ourselves.82
2.101. That supreme yogi embraced [me]; "Obtain the sadguru!" he said commandingly (?).83
2.102. Our voice choked, we could say nothing; … (??) all the bhavas we expressed by bhava [alone].84
2.103. Worshipping [his] feet, seeing [his] divine radiance and obtaining the guru's grace, I became happy.
2.104. Thus we asked about the tattva of Radha; we asked about the tattva of the Divine Couple, Radha and Krishna.
2.105. The guru's grace came, great merit became mine: [I,] the lowly one, heard words from the guru's holy mouth.
2.106. My guru, … (??), the all-auspicious, said: "We shall give you initiation (diksha)."85
2.107. Thus the supreme guru rejoiced; giving [me] the great mantras, he gave [me] satisfaction.
2.108. He is my diksha-guru, the trust of the world; the mantra of Radha [and] the tattva of Radha [he gave me] into the ear (?), in secret.86
2.109. Such secret words he spoke; he declared plainly: "Bhava is the form of Radha.87
2.110. The manifestation of bhava is the sight of Radha; absorption in bhava is the union of the Couple."
2.111. "What is bhava?" I asked the guru; "I [wish to] hear the secret tattvas," I said.88
2.112. My guru, firm (?) in absorption in bhava, said: "We shall bring [you] to Radha (lit. 'let [you] meet in Radha's company')."89
2.113. Near the guru's ashrama there was a well; the guru said: "Now look well (?) at that well."90

Ganga in the well; the darshan of Radha; the end of Prabhu's account; the questions of Ramananda and Svarupa about the gopis and the form of radiance

2.114"In that well is, in person, the abode of Ganga; go and bathe: going [there] is the way to contentment (?)."91
2.115. With a pure mind I went and entered the well; there I saw Bhagirathi (?) in person.
2.116. The Mother is seated on a makara seat; in a raised (?) hand She holds a lotus.92
2.117. Carefully She holds in Her hand a … pot (??). At the sight of that Lady, the Remover of sins,93
2.118. my mind melted, bhava arose; immersed in bhava, heart and mind became still (?).94
2.119. Having finished bathing, I carefully returned and bowed to both feet of the guru.
2.120. Streams of tears flowed from my eyes; Krishna's name came forth unceasingly from my mouth.
2.121. Thus my heart was stunned in bhava; without the guru's grace who (?) would have become steady?95
2.122. The guru's grace came, my sorrow went away; I obtained the darshan of Radha, full of bhava.96
2.123. "Know: this bhava is the essence among the prakritis; She in person is Radha, the measure of prakriti.97
2.124. Meditating in bhava, one will surely meet Krishna; without bhava one will never attain the Accepter of bhava.98
2.125. Immersed in bhava, meditate always (??); in bhava ever worship (?) Radha, full of rasa.99
2.126. When He Himself (??) appears as an avatara in bhava (??), only then will [people] obtain the darshan of Krishnachandra."100
2.127. Having heard this account of Radha's tattva from the guru's mouth, I have set forth this mahabhava again.101
2.128. After this Raya Ramananda asked: "If bhava is Radha, then who are the gopis?"102
2.129. Hearing these words, Chaitanya Thakur smiled gently and … (??) calmly (?).103
2.130. He said: "Among the devotees you are My chief; your mind has thickened (?) in the great rasa of Krishna."104
2.131. Having spoken (?) thus, Prabhu, the moon of Nadia, said: "Let Us set forth the secret of the gopis."105
2.132. Then Ramananda became eager; with folded hands he humbly entreated Prabhu.
2.133. [Prabhu] said: "[She is] in the form of bhava, in the form of consciousness (?)," and again set forth the tattva (?) and qualities of Sri Radha.106
2.134. Hearing [this], they felt the thrill (??) in their bodies (?) increase; the devotees obtained welfare.107
2.135. "To this there is one more doubt," Svarupa (?) … (??) set forth to Prabhu:108
2.136. "You are the avatara in person; the form of bhava, the mahabhava, the bee (?) of prakriti.109
2.137. We have directly obtained the mercy of Krishnachandra; You, Prabhu, bear the name Deliverer of devotees.
2.138. Gosai, Lover of devotees, be merciful for once: how is one to remember (?) the great Queen whose form is radiance?110
2.139. How did the form of radiance arise? Telling this, dispel (?) my doubt."111
2.140. Hearing the devotee's words, Prabhu, the crest-jewel of devotees, spoke smilingly, considering the essence (??) of bhava.112
2.141. Prabhu said gently (?) to the devotees … (??): "Listen, O devotees: the radiance …113
2.142. Once … (??) by the Jahnavi (?), in the abode (?) of Madana (?), eight … (??) met together (?)."114

Surya's austerity; Krishna asks for his radiance; Vrishabhanu and Kirttida; Radha full of radiance; Ramananda's question about the gopis again

2.143Day by day (?) his austerity grew ever heavier; the radiance of the gods was eclipsed (?).115
2.144. Then Narayana (??), the Lord Krishnachandra, Devendra (?), appeared before Surya.116
2.145. Granting words of fearlessness, He asked a question: "For what reason, O Vedanga (?), have you practised austerity?"117
2.146. He said: "O Bhanu, you are the light of the world; if you become hidden, the world will perish (?)."118
2.147. The Lord full of radiance, the ocean of mercy, said: "For what reason (?) do you practise severe austerity?"
2.148. Then Savitar (?) said: "O (?) Hrishikesha! My radiance has become heavy, has become too weighty (?).119
2.149. My radiance has brought me affliction; it has seemed to me unbearable.
2.150. O Madana! You appeared [to me,] Bhanu (?), [but] did not take away the radiance, Lord — You made me heavy.120
2.151. You do not take away my radiance …; why then, knowing everything, do You ask again, O Guru?121
2.152. Take away my radiance, Lord full of radiance! You are infinite, imperishable (?), the support of the world."
2.153. Hearing this, the Supreme Krishna was pleased …122
2.154. "Becoming incarnate, give Me [your] radiances …123
2.155. Your radiances are My play-companions; I will be with them, making love.
2.156. She will live in the world (?) as your daughter; all will know [her] as My wife (?).124
2.157. I will appear in Vraja, in the settlement of Gokula; you will hand over to Me the daughter full of radiance."
2.158. Having said this, the Lord vanished. The radiant Bhanu (?) was born under the name Vrishabhanu.125
2.159. His wife is the lovely Kirttida; then from the womb (?) of Kirttida the radiance appeared (lit. "was born").126
2.160. Because [all] were amazed, they gave [Her] the name "dha"; by [the syllable] "ra" (?), [denoting] radiance, the name became "Radha".127
2.161. My Radha, full of radiance, who appeared (lit. "was born") from the radiance of the Sun, became famous in the world under the name Radha.128
2.162. From that day (?) the play of Krishna and Radha took place; the name "Radha-Krishna" … (??) this world.129
2.163. Of the form of Bhavamayi you had heard before (?); now you have come to know the form of Tejomayi.130
2.164. As you heard the name of Radha [in the words] "preyasi-yam yatha radha", so you have realised the … (??) of Radha and Krishna:131
"As [dear to Me] is this beloved Radha, so dear to Me are My devotees;
the two-syllable name 'Krishna' together (?) with [the name] of Radha … (??)."132
2.165. Having said so much, the Supreme Gosai fell silent; He at once (?) stopped (?) the stream of sweet speech.133
2.166. The devotees, seeing for a moment the … (??) of Prabhu, shed streams of tears and at once came to their senses.134
2.167. After this Raya Ramananda asked: "If bhava is Radha, then who are the gopis?"135
2.168. Hearing these words, Chaitanya Thakur smiled (?) a gentle smile and with most sweet speech
2.169. said: "Among the devotees you (?) are my chief; may your mind remain ever immersed in the rasa of Krishna."

The secret of the eight gopis: the nine "moons" of bhava and Radha's sakhis

2.170Having spoken thus, Prabhu, the moon of Nadia (?), [said]: "Listen (?) then to the secret of the gopis from beginning to end.136
2.171. She who is in the form of mahabhava is Krishna's beloved; bhava is Radha, mahabhava is the beauty (?) of the gopis.137
2.172. Know bhava: [in it] abides this (?) nine-petalled moon; in the distinction of the nine moons bhava becomes manifest.138
2.173. The essence of the nine moons is the moon full of all-bliss: [it is] the manifestation of Radha, full of all-bliss.139
2.174. Radha … (??) of the moon of all-bliss — always in [Her] form (?) She … (??) bliss.140
2.175. We shall surely disclose the secret of the eight gopis and make your minds understand mahabhava.
2.176. Understand this endless greatness of the eight sakhis, whose end even the king of the gods himself does not know.141
2.177. The dweller of the moon that bestows all perfections — know: [her] name is Guptagudhi (??); [she is] lovely Lalita.142
2.178. Know: there is the moon that removes all diseases; she who, in secret, by name, has appeared (?) again —143
2.179. named Vrindavati, the essence of the gopis, the goddess who removes Krishna's troubles, a treasury of prema.144
2.180. Know: there stands the moon that protects all; there in person, know, abides Vishakha.145
2.181. The goddess Vishakha, of supreme nature (?), enchanting, bestowing confidence (?) on the gopis, dweller of the forest.146
2.182. The moon that accomplishes all aims — after it (?) the bright (??) [moon], where the sakhi Chandravati (?) eternally enjoys.147
2.183. [She] is by nature sampradaya (?), sporting in enjoyment; beautiful, merciful, the enchantress of Krishna.148
2.184. Madana-manjari is the embodiment of universal good fortune; cherishing the moon of good fortune, she roams (?).149
2.185. This great sakhi is born in the high (?) kala; the fair-faced maiden is named Kulakaula.150
2.186. The name of another sakhi is … (??); she guards the moon that agitates all.151
2.187. Her shakti is Nigarbha, the supreme yogini, bestowing great contentment, the enchantress of Tripura (?).152
2.188. The sakhi named … (??), very tender, is a playful young maiden who fulfils all … (??).153
2.189. … (??) rahasya is her good quality; … (??) brings (?) the desired (?) form (??) … (??) again.154
2.190. Saubhagyavati is [Radha's] companion, very skilful, the enchantress of the three worlds; she holds the moon.155
2.191. The sakhi whose quality is the parapara (??) rahasya, going (?) to Krishna's secret, is skilled among the devotees (?).156
2.192. Thus the gopis surround (??) Radha; the bhava of eightfold bhakti … (?) … …157
2.193. The eight sakhis again (?) in bhava (?) worship in the ninefold way; skilfully (?) they make bhava — love for Krishna.158
2.194. Bhava is manifest by the name of mahabhava; in it (?) the mind of Krishna, the Son [of Nanda], remains immersed.159
2.195. One who thus contemplates the bhava of the gopis penetrates in secret the essence of Krishna's rasa.160
2.196. He obtains the highest good — the feet (?) of Krishna …161
2.197. A Vaishnava who has penetrated the tattva — the essence of Krishna's rasa — if he tastes (?) this in bhava, obtains the Friend.162

The end of Prabhu's teaching on the gopis; the devotees' plea; the author's conclusion

2.198That (?) is the essence of both worlds, this one and the next; this rasa of the Supreme Krishna is deep (?).163
2.199. [She] is the good of the world, the giver (?) of Krishna's life, in the form of the bride (?) of the devotees' hearts.164
2.200. Fixing the mind at the feet of Sri Krishnachandra wholly unshaken (?), [the devotee] will worship (?) unshaken through the nine divisions of bhava."165
2.201. Thus [Prabhu] spoke tender words gently; opening His eyes (?), Gosai looked (?) at the devotees.166
2.202. From the corners (?) of [their] eyes a stream of tears flows: "We are Prabhu's servants, worthless slaves.167
2.203. In the company of Bhava-Radha there is no meeting with Him (?) for us; how then shall we obtain the Lord of Sri Radha?168
2.204. We are … (??), all of us, as many as we are, lowly; the mercy of Chaitanyachandra is our only strength.169
2.205. Without His mercy our life is in vain; the good of the world is He, Chaitanya Himself."
2.206. Enchanted (?) by that guru Gauranga, my mind is unshaken; may it remain thus (?) … (??) at the foot of Nilachala.170
2.207. He is the cause (?) of the universe, the Lord of Niladri; may this time, this dreadful entanglement [of worldly life], pass in [His] service.171
2.208. What I heard from the mouth of guru Gauranga — that mahabhava I … (??) and wrote down.172
2.209. The devotee-friends (?), forgiving my faults, will come to know the Bhava-prakasha, recognising the guru's feet.173
2.210. Kanhai, lowly and worthless, seeks refuge; the song of Chaitanya, [Lord] of the universe (?), in the [vernacular] tongue (?) … (??) Kanhai (?).174
Thus [ends] the second vritta (?) of the Mahabhava-prakasha — the description of the nectar of the narratives of Sri Mahaprabhu.175

Notes

  1. The chapter heading is printed ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ବୃନ୍ତ (dwitīẏa bṛnta). As in the colophon at the end of Chapter 1 (after 1.158), the word ବୃନ୍ତ (literally "stalk") is understood as "vritta, section" (perhaps for ବୃତ୍ତ, bṛtta). Chapter 2 begins with this heading, and the numbering of the couplets starts again from 1.
  2. Purushottama-kshetra is Puri. The Panchakroshi is the sacred district of five kroshas around the holy place. Bentapur (ବେଣ୍ଟପୁର, beṇṭapura) is a village near Puri; Kanai places Ramananda Raya's family here (2.4–2.10).
  3. Karana (karaṇa) is the Odia caste of scribes and officials; karaṇam (in southern Odisha and among the Telugu) is a village accountant-scribe. Panjias (pāñjiā) are keepers of records (pāñji, "register, chronicle"). Printed ≈ କରଣମ ନେ (karaṇama ne) with a space; apparently the sign ା failed to print, and the reading should be କରଣମାନେ (karaṇamāne, "the Karanas", plural: cf. "in their family" in 2.5). The word ଚରମ (carama, "foremost"? "last"?) is read with doubt.

  137. Printed ରୂପେଣୀ; given as ରୂପିଣୀ (rūpiṇī, "in the form"). The last word is printed ≈ ଶୋଭ (the ା sign is damaged); taken as ଶୋଭା (śobhā, "beauty, adornment"). On Radha as bhava cf. 2.109–2.110 and the note to 2.109.
  138. From this couplet Kanai speaks of nine "moons" (ଚନ୍ଦ, canda) and of the sakhis connected with each of them. The epithets of the moons coincide with the names of the nine enclosures (āvaraṇa) of the Sri-chakra, the yantra of Shakta tantra (the Sri-vidya school): "full of all-bliss" (sarvānandamaya, 2.173–2.174), "bestowing all perfections" (sarva-siddhi-prada, 2.177), "removing all diseases" (sarva-roga-hara, 2.178), "protecting all" (sarva-rakṣā-kara, 2.180), "accomplishing all aims" (sarvārtha-sādhaka, 2.182), "[bestowing] universal good fortune" (sarva-saubhāgya, 2.184), "agitating all" (sarva-saṅkṣobhaṇa, 2.186), apparently "fulfilling all hopes" (sarvāśā-paripūraka, 2.188) and "enchanting the three worlds" (trailokya-mohana, 2.190); the names and epithets of the sakhis recall the names of the classes of yoginis of the same enclosures: "manifest" and "secret" (prakaṭa, gupta, 2.177–2.178), sampradāya (2.183), kula-kaula (2.185), nigarbha (2.187), rahasya and parāpara-rahasya (2.189, 2.191), and also the name of Tripura (2.187). Gaudiya Vaishnavas (following Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) do not combine the lila of Radha and Krishna with tantric schemes and practices: Radha's sakhis are expansions of Her own nature (kāya-vyūha, Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 4), and their service is pure prema in Vraja. The word ≈ ଚନ୍ଦେଟି (candeṭi) is taken as "this moon" (canda eṭi?).

  140. The word ≈ ଭ୍ରମୟୀ (bhramaẏī) is not identified (possibly ଭାବମୟୀ, bhābamaẏī, "full of bhava", cf. 2.122). ବିଗ୍ରହରେ (bigrahare, "in form, in body"): in this type the sign ି is often given as a curl inside ବ (likewise in 2.181, 2.183, 2.184); after ସେହୁ (sehu, "she") the word ≈ ମେ is not identified.
  141. The king of the gods (debarāja) is Indra.
  142. The name is printed ≈ ଗୁପ୍ତାଗ + ଢ଼ୀ, with the sign ୂ shifted below the line; taken as ଗୁପ୍ତାଗୂଢ଼ୀ (guptāgūṛhī, "Secret-Hidden"). Lalita is the first of Radha's eight principal sakhis (cf. 2.45 and the note to it).
  143. ଅଛୁ (achu, "is, abides") is a form in ‑achu, here and in 2.180. The second half is taken as the beginning of a sentence that continues in 2.179: "she who in secret … has appeared again, named Vrindavati". The word ≈ ପ୍ରକଟିଛୁ (prakaṭichu, "has appeared") is read tentatively.
  144. Vrindavati is apparently Vrinda (Vrinda-devi), the goddess of the forest of Vrindavana; in the Chaitanya-charitamrita and among Gaudiya Vaishnavas she arranges the lilas of Radha and Krishna but is not counted among the eight principal sakhis.   145. Printed ≈ ଶାଖାଟି, preceded by a fragment of a letter; given as ବିଶାଖାଟି (biśākhāṭi, "Vishakha"; ‑ṭi is a classifier). Vishakha is the second of the eight principal sakhis (cf. 2.45 and the note to it).
  146. ପର ସ୍ୱରୂପିଣୀ (para swarūpiṇī) is taken as "of supreme nature"; the editor's note mark "(୧)" after the word is omitted. ଦମ୍ଭ (dambha) is "pride, confidence"; the sense "bestowing confidence on the gopis" is uncertain.
  147. The last word of the first half is printed unclearly (≈ ଶୁ + ଭ with a subscript sign); taken as ଶୁଭ୍ର (śubhra, "bright"); there is no rhyme with ଭୋଗ (bhoga). ଅନ୍ତେ (ante) is "at the end, then".   148. First word: ସ and ଂ are fused (the sign resembles ଫ); read as ସଂପ୍ରଦାୟା (saṁpradāẏā). ବିଳାସିନୀ is printed with ି as a curl inside ବ (cf. the note to 2.174). ସୁନ୍ଦରୀ (sundarī, "beautiful") may also be the name of a sakhi.
  149. Madana-manjari is a name (cf. the manjaris, Radha's young maidservants, among Gaudiya Vaishnavas). The first word of the second half is ବ with a curl + ହରଇ; taken as ବିହରଇ (biharaï, "roams, sports").
  150. The first letter of the first word is ଉ or ଜ; taken as ଉଚ୍ଚ (ucca, "high"). A kala is a sixteenth digit of the moon. Kulakaula is the name of a sakhi; "kula" and "kaula" are terms of tantric schools.
  151. The name is printed ≈ ମ + a letter resembling ଥ + ା (the same letter occurs in the name in 2.188); not identified.
  152. Printed ନଗର୍ଭା without ି; given as ନିଗର୍ଭା (nigarbhā). ତ୍ରିପୁର ମୋହିନୀ (tripura mohinī) is taken as "the enchantress of Tripura (?)"; Tripura (Tripurasundari) is the goddess of the Sri-chakra in Shakta tantra (cf. the note to 2.172).
  153. The name is printed ≈ ଚି (or ବି) with a curl, a small letter and ଥା; possibly ଚିତ୍ରା (citrā, Chitra, one of Radha's eight sakhis). Second half: printed ≈ ସର୍ବ ଶାପ ପୂରେ (sarba śāpa pūre, "fulfils all curses"?); by sense and by the series of Sri-chakra epithets (cf. the note to 2.172) one would expect ସର୍ବ ଆଶା ପୂରେ (sarba āśā pūre, "fulfils all hopes").   154. The line is read only in part: the first word ≈ ମସ୍ତପର is not identified (possibly one of the names of rahasya, "secret", "supreme secret", cf. the note to 2.172); ≈ ବାଞ୍ଛିତ (bāñchita, "desired"), ≈ ରୂପ (rūpa, "form"), ≈ ଆଣଇ (āṇaï, "brings"), ≈ ମୀରତଲେ (not identified; possibly ପୀରତିଲେ, "if one loves").
  155. "Saubhagyavati" ("fortunate") may also be an epithet. ସୁଚତୁରୀ (sucaturī) is "very skilful". "Enchanting the three worlds" — cf. the note to 2.172.
  156. The first word is printed ≈ ମରା‑ାର + a fused letter; taken as ପରାପର (parāpara, "higher and lower"), cf. the note to 2.172. Printed ଗ, a gap, ମିନୀ; given as ଗାମିନୀ (gāminī, "going"). ଭକ୍ତରେ (bhaktare) is "among the devotees" or "in bhakti".
  157. ≈ ଏମ'ନ is taken as ଏମନ୍ତ (emanta, "thus"). The last word of the first half, ≈ ସୀଢ଼ନ୍ତି, is not identified; by sense possibly ବେଢ଼ନ୍ତି (beṛhanti, "surround", cf. 2.42).   158. Ninefold bhakti — the nine kinds of devotional service (hearing, chanting, remembering, etc., Srimad-Bhagavatam 7.5.23). ପୀରତି (pīrati) is the popular form of ପ୍ରୀତି (prīti, "love"). The words ≈ ପୁଣ (puṇa), ≈ ଭାବ (bhāba) and ≈ ନିପୁଣେ (nipuṇe) are read tentatively.
  159. କେବଣ (kebaṇa, "which") is taken as "in which"; ନନ୍ଦନ (nandana) is "the Son [of Nanda]", an epithet of Krishna.
  160. Printed ଯ without େ; given as ଯେ (ye, "who"). ଏମନେ = ଏମନ୍ତେ (emante, "thus"). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching one can enter the lila of Radha and Krishna only by following the sakhis (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 8, Prabhu's conversation with Ramananda Raya).
  161. Only the first half is printed (the line ends with "।"); the second half of the couplet is missing in the edition. The words ≈ ଚରଣ (caraṇa, "feet") and ≈ ସେ (se, "he") are printed indistinctly.
  162. The sign "।" between the halves is not printed (supplied by the norm). Printed ପ, a gap, ନ; given as ପାନ (pāna, "drinking"): "if he drinks this" is taken as "tastes [the rasa]". "The Friend" (bāndhaba, "friend, kinsman") is apparently Krishna.
  163. Prabhu's teaching on the secret of the gopis (2.170–2.197) continues. "That" is apparently the rasa of Krishna spoken of in 2.195–2.197.   164. The feminine epithets (kāriṇī, swarūpiṇī) point to a feminine subject — apparently the bhava of the gopis, that is, Radha (cf. 2.171: "bhava is Radha"). The word ≈ କାରିଣୀ (kāriṇī, "she who makes") is read with doubt (the sign ରି resembles ଶ). The word ≈ ବଧୂ (badhū, "bride, consort") is printed with an unclear subscript sign; possibly ବିଧୁ (bidhu, "moon") or ବନ୍ଧୁ (bandhu, "friend").
  165. The nine divisions of bhava — cf. the "ninefold" bhakti in 2.193 (cf. the note to 2.193). Printed run together ଭାବନବଧା. The word ≈ ସୁନିଶ୍ଚଳେ (suniścaḷe, "wholly unshaken") is read by sense and rhyme: the superscript sign is unclear. ≈ ଭଜିବ (bhajiba, "will worship") is read with doubt. Prabhu's speech apparently ends here.
  166. Cf. 1.142–1.143 and 2.165–2.166: absorbed in bhava, Prabhu closes His eyes. The word ≈ ନେତ୍ର (netra, "eyes") is read by sense: the second letter resembles ସ. The last word is printed ≈ ଚୁହିଁଲେ (no ା visible); understood as ଚାହିଁଲେ (cāhi̐le, "looked").
  167. From 2.202 to 2.205 the speakers are apparently the devotees; direct speech is not marked in the text, and its limits are set by sense. The word ≈ କୋଣୁ (koṇu, "from the corners") is read with doubt.
  168. "Bhava-Radha" — cf. 2.171. The first half-line is understood with doubt: "we have no access to the company of Radha-bhava". The Lord of Sri Radha is Krishna. In Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching one enters the lila of Radha and Krishna by following the sakhis (cf. the note to 2.195), and attains this by the mercy of Sri Chaitanya — Krishna Himself united with Radha's bhava (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 1.5); cf. 2.204–2.205.
  169. The word is not identified: printed ≈ ଦୁ + କ୍ର + ର (or ତ) + ଣୀ; possibly a corrupted word meaning "sinners" (cf. ଦୁଷ୍କୃତୀ, duṣkṛtī).
  170. From 2.206 the author speaks himself (cf. 1.144–1.158). Kanai calls Sri Chaitanya his guru (cf. 2.208). Here and in 2.208 ଗୌରଙ୍ଗ is printed without ା; ଗୌରାଙ୍ଗ is given (cf. the same correction in the edition's errata for p. 17). ଭୁଲେ (bhule) is understood as "enchanted" (bhulibā — "to forget; to be enchanted"). The word ≈ ଦପ୍ରିମ is not identified (printed ≈ ଦ, then ପ with a subscript sign and an arc above, then ମ); ≈ ଏତିକ (etika, "thus, just so") is read with doubt. Nilachala is Puri (cf. the note to 1.1).
  171. "He" — by the link with 2.206, apparently Gauranga, whom Kanai praises as the Lord of Niladri, that is, identifies with Jagannatha; it may also be a separate praise of Jagannatha. Gaudiya Vaishnavas worship Jagannatha as Krishna Himself, and Sri Chaitanya as Krishna who has taken on the mood and complexion of Radha (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 1.5; Madhya 8); oneness in tattva does not mean that one dissolves into the other. ≈ କରଣ (karaṇa, "cause, maker") is understood as = କାରଣ (kāraṇa). The final «॥» is not printed (given by the norm).
  172. The word is not identified: printed ≈ ମ, a dot, ସ; possibly ମସି (masi, "ink": "wrote down in ink") or ମାସ (māsa, "month"). Cf. 1.144: "taking up the pen, I set it down in writing". ଶୁଣିଲ and ଲେଖିଲ are printed without a final ି; these are first-person forms ("I heard", "I wrote down").
  173. Bhava-prakasha is a short title of the poem (cf. 1.150, 1.158). ଗୁରୁପଦ is corrected to ଗୁରୁପାଦ (gurupāda, "the guru's feet") per the edition's errata ("୧୪।୧୨"; the line number matches our count). The word ≈ ବାନ୍ଧବଗଣ (bāndhabagaṇa, "friends, kin") is read with doubt: the second letter is a conjunct with a slanting stroke (ନ୍ଧ?).
  174. The author's signature (bhanita), as in 1.158 (cf. the note to 1.158). The second half-line is understood with doubt: ବ୍ରହ୍ମାଣ୍ଡ ଚୈତନ୍ୟ (brahmāṇḍa caitanya) — "Chaitanya, [Lord] of the universe" or "the consciousness of the universe"; ଗୀତ ଭାଷା (gīta bhāṣā) — "a song in the [vernacular] tongue"?; the word ≈ ତଦେ is not identified.
